feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: clear positioning, relevant progression, and solid evidence of scope across web, content, analytics, and multimedia. It reads professionally, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and career progression align well with digital strategy/communications leadership.  
- Strong credibility through concrete scope indicators: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers,” and named tools/platforms.  
- Broad yet coherent skill set spanning strategy, CMS/web operations, analytics, governance, and multimedia production.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more results, not just responsibilities: include measurable outcomes such as traffic growth, email performance, engagement lifts, cost savings, process efficiencies, or campaign impact.  
- Reduce duplication and tighten structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to avoid repetition and save space.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: use “12 years of experience” (missing “of”); standardize serial commas (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs versions without final comma); consider “front-end” consistently; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary filler. No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and foregrounding mission-driven digital leadership would make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard phrasing.
- Replace broad lists with a more focused value proposition tied to senior-level leadership, digital transformation, and mission-driven organizations.
- Add scale or context from recent roles where possible, e.g., enterprise web platforms, cross-functional teams, or advocacy-focused audiences.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, CMS modernization, editorial workflow design, and digital governance. Strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear, audience-focused content and aligning stakeholders around effective advocacy and communications goals.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap heavily with Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” and stakeholder coordination are reinforced throughout Work Experience, so avoid overloading the intro with both.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize higher-value leadership and systems strengths rather than broad phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms like “Multi-channel communication” with more specific, senior-level phrasing such as “Cross-channel communications leadership.”
- Align wording with the strongest evidence in recent roles: digital transformation, CMS/platform modernization, editorial governance, analytics, and advocacy communications.
- Reduce operational overlap by combining similar items like “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS modernization • Editorial systems & governance • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially duplicates the header summary and Topline Skills; consider shortening it or using it only for broad themes not listed elsewhere.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also overlaps with Soft Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical breadth, but it reads as a task list and overlaps with your NACo entries on governance, workflows, and web operations. Tighten it around distinctive consulting impact, platform modernization, and the AI search initiative.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client value: “Embedded full-time as a strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, campaign platform development, and enterprise web improvements.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into sharper outcomes: combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet focused on improving cross-channel coordination and operational efficiency.
- Make the Drupal work more results-oriented: “Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including microsites, modular content components, and member toolkits.” Add metrics if possible: launch volume, traffic, engagement, time-to-publish, or stakeholder adoption.
- Elevate the most distinctive item: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and discovery UX.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” repeats NACo language; reframe around consulting outcomes.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may duplicate skills sections unless tied to a business result.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals; it will be stronger if you tighten the opening and add clearer outcomes from the redesign, analytics, and studio build. Emphasize enterprise leadership here and leave more operational detail to the earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad opening with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Tighten bullets around major wins: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add outcome language where possible: improved engagement, reduced publishing bottlenecks, faster reporting, lower vendor spend, increased in-house production capacity, or stronger campaign performance.
- Reframe channels bullet to show leadership impact, not just reach: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials; aligned channels to advocacy, events, and member communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video/programming bullets overlap with the Associate Director and Digital Media Manager roles; focus this entry on scaling/building the studio, not recurring production.
- Governance/workflow language also appears elsewhere; keep this version strategic and organization-wide.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good scope, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later NACo director role and earlier digital media role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel ownership, and any concrete growth or production outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope line: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social, and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and cross-team editorial execution.”
- Replace “helping” phrasing with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: newsletter open/click rates, audience growth, video cadence/views, publishing volume, or turnaround improvements.
- Tighten bullets to focus on what changed under you: “Launched/expanded a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel” and “Built editorial planning workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams to improve publishing consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthened editorial planning/workflows” overlaps with the 2022–2024 NACo role; keep this version focused on implementation rather than governance.
- Weekly video/newsletter work also echoes the 2015–2018 role; clarify scale or ownership increased here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/freelance experience. Make it sharper, more senior, and slightly more outcome-oriented by emphasizing governance, transformation, and mission-driven/public-sector leadership.

Suggested edit
- Replace generic phrases with tighter, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “content planning” for “content operations” or “transformation,” which better reflects your recent leadership scope.
- Keep terminology consistent with the rest of the CV: use “cross-channel” instead of “multi-channel” to match the header.
- If space allows, prioritize the most differentiating items first: strategy, governance, public-sector/policy, then audience focus.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” repeat ideas already stated in the header/Core Competencies.
- “Editorial systems and governance” is close to “Editorial workflow design”; choose one framing to avoid dilution.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s currently a mixed keyword list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. Make it more selective and higher-level so it reinforces recent impact rather than repeating tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal & enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • SharePoint & Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery
- Lead with Drupal/CMS modernization and AI-enabled search, since those are most supported by the most recent roles.
- Group coding skills into one phrase instead of listing each separately; this reads more senior and saves space.
- If possible, replace “Airtable systems” with a more outcome-oriented phrase like “Airtable workflow systems” or “content operations systems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills strategic/high-level and leave tool-by-tool detail to Technical + IT.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies (“Workflow & systems architecture”).

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack that aligns with the most recent NACo and consulting work, but it reads as a generic keyword list. Tighten it around outcomes and decision-making value, not just platforms.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, BigQuery, Looker Studio and Power BI for KPI design, executive reporting and digital performance optimization.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “executive reporting” or “decision-ready reporting” for sharper, more standard wording.
- Consider swapping “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, audience behavior and conversion analysis” if accurate; it sounds more strategic and specific.
- Optional rewrite: “Analytics stack: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, BigQuery, Looker Studio and Power BI • KPI design • Executive dashboards • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and the NACo bullet on expanding analytics infrastructure; keep this section concise and tool-forward rather than repeating impact claims.
- If space is tight, drop either “KPI design” or “executive reporting” since both imply reporting strategy.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Livestreaming

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies and multiple NACo bullets. Make it more specific to current/recent strengths and tools, not broad category labels.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize delivery scope and technical depth: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera operation and switching • Studio buildout and operations”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a sharper phrase if true: “End-to-end video production” or “Video production, editing, and live switching”
- Consider adding one higher-value capability instead of a generic item: “Virtual event platform production” or “Run-of-show and technical coordination”
- If space allows, align with recent impact from NACo: “In-house studio production” rather than just “Studio operations”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This repeats “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies; keep one broad version there and make this list more technical/specific.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “Livestreaming”; differentiate or combine.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In this lower-priority technical section, make it tighter and emphasize the most relevant/recent platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest evidence and recency: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider leading with Drupal and separating lighter-use tools.
- If accurate, add proficiency context instead of just names: “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Consider trimming GitHub Pages if it was incidental compared with Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint work.
- Keep this item platform-only; save implementation detail for the coding/technical line.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills entry almost exactly; consider removing one or changing this to “CMS Platforms.”
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support your most recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Technical integrations: APIs, Google Tag Manager • Deployment & automation: GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) if space is tight: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner and equally credible.
- Group by function rather than listing flat tools; this makes the section feel more senior and aligned with your recent consulting/director roles.
- If accurate, add one specificity cue tied to impact elsewhere in the CV, e.g. “for Drupal-based sites” or “for campaign/microsite builds.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; consider removing them from one section.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may partially overlap with GitHub Actions here.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with stronger positioning already established in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a pure list to a capability-led label, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems.”
- Prioritize tools tied to recent, higher-value work: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana; move chat tools to the end or remove.
- Add brief functional grouping for clarity: “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Teams.”
- If space allows, connect to outcomes indirectly: “workflow automation, editorial coordination, project tracking” rather than listing every platform equally.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same idea verbatim here.
- Slack and Teams are common collaboration tools and may dilute the stronger systems/automation focus unless they are central to the role.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should stay concise and emphasize platform breadth rather than repeat channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform names for readability: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope/strength via parenthetical specialization rather than a full sentence: e.g., campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation
- Keep ordering by strongest/recently used platform first; if Dynamics 365 is most current, leave first, otherwise reorder to match recent hands-on use

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters” or “led email strategy” here; those are already covered in Work Experience
- Don’t repeat analytics or workflow language from other Technical + IT / Topline Skills sections

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Tighten it to emphasize foundational contributions, promotion, and any measurable outputs without repeating later leadership achievements.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and scope: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social, and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence/audience for weekly videos, or workflow improvements (e.g., turnaround time, publishing consistency).
- Clarify your contribution level with stronger verbs: “helped launch,” “produced,” “coordinated,” “streamlined,” “mentored” instead of “supported” and “contributed.”
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social, and multimedia production. Helped deliver a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day publishing workflows while mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launch/build phase rather than channel ownership.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already used more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around concrete outputs so it complements, rather than repeats, the later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the strongest differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast…”
- Replace broad phrases like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with clearer scope or audience impact.
- Split policy/research support from multimedia work so both read as intentional contributions.
- If possible, add volume or reach: number of episodes, stakeholders supported, programs served, or types of materials produced.

Suggested edit:
- Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program teams and policy communications.
- Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational campaigns and member-facing materials.
- Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, production, and rollout.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid emphasizing general digital/media support too heavily; later NACo roles already cover web, video, and channel management in more depth.
- Don’t reuse “cross-channel communications” or workflow language here unless tied to a distinct accomplishment.
